title: The banyan in the seed
hookLine: Uddalaka has his son break open a banyan seed, and Samkhya argues the effect is already in its cause
carry: the effect already lives in its cause
tomorrow: Why would the seer and the world ever meet?

cards: In the Chandogya Upanishad, a young man named Shvetaketu comes home after twelve years of study, quite pleased with himself.
His father, Uddalaka, asks him one question his teachers never covered, and the son can't answer it. So the father teaches him at home. Bring me a fruit from that banyan tree, he says.
Break it. What do you see? Tiny seeds, sir.
Break one of those. What do you see now? Nothing at all, sir.

teach.h: THE TREE WAS IN THE SEED.
teach.b: And the father says, in paraphrase: that fine essence you can't see, my son, is what this whole great banyan stands on. The tree was already in the seed.
Earlier in the same lesson he asks a sharper question: how could something that is come from what is not?

teach.h: SAT KARYAM: THE EFFECT ALREADY IS.
teach.b: Centuries later the Samkhya Karika turned that kind of intuition into an argument, and named it in one verse: sat karyam, the effect already is. That's satkarya.
Its reasons: nothing comes from what doesn't exist at all; you need the right material; not everything comes from everything.
Commentators give an example still used in classrooms: press sesame and you get oil, press sand all day and you get none.
The old teachers also point to milk becoming curd, and Nani's kitchen still shows it: a spoon of yesterday's curd in warm milk, one quiet night, and by morning, dahi. Nobody built it. It unfolded.
So for Samkhya, creation isn't something out of nothing. The whole world was folded inside prakriti, the root, and it unfolds. Not every Hindu school agrees.

teach.h: NYAYA SAYS: THE POT IS NEW.
teach.b: Nyaya and Vaisheshika argue a pot is a genuinely new thing, and the tradition keeps both arguments in the room.
Uddalaka takes the seed somewhere Samkhya won't follow: that fine essence, he says, is the self of the whole world, and you are that.
Many teachers draw one lesson from both: what you will become isn't bolted on from outside. It's already in you, waiting for its conditions.

how: Students of Indian philosophy learn the debate over causation, Samkhya's view that the effect pre-exists in its cause against the Nyaya-Vaisheshika view that it is newly made, and the Chandogya's banyan seed is told in homes and classrooms as a picture of the unseen essence.

o: a manual of recipes for festival sweets
a hymn praising the potter who shapes the world
verses arguing the effect is already in its cause

games.q: the effect in the cause — tap the pairs.
p: nothing seen, the whole tree inside
the pot is a new thing

s: Samkhya says creation is making something out of nothing
for Samkhya, the world unfolds from prakriti, where it was already folded.
in the Chandogya, Shvetaketu breaks a banyan seed and sees nothing inside
and his father says the whole great tree stands on that unseen essence.
every Hindu school accepts Samkhya's view of cause and effect
Nyaya and Vaisheshika argue the effect is something new.

games.q: you're a Samkhya teacher. a student asks: before the potter shapes the clay, does the pot exist?
o: no, the pot is completely new.
yes, hidden in the clay, waiting to be shown.
games.why: Samkhya says the effect is already in its material cause; making it is unfolding it. Nyaya and Vaisheshika answer the other way.

practice: Sit comfortably and picture the banyan seed, broken open, nothing to see inside.

Bring to mind one beginning in your life right now, a friendship, a habit, a hope, and look at it the way Uddalaka looked at the seed: the whole tree already folded in. With each out-breath, let it rest there.
If you pray, you can hold that beginning in prayer.

wordCard.voice: The Samkhya Karika. Its argument on causes: the effect already exists in its cause, so the world unfolds from prakriti instead of appearing from nothing.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the view that the effect already exists in its cause; Samkhya's answer on causation.

carryVoice: Your line: the effect already lives in its cause. The banyan was in the seed. See you tomorrow.
